svg.title: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean commits and no secrets: two secret scans started at the same time each block the password from a container of their own
svg.text: the framework guards what reaches the repository: clean
Scenario: two secret scans started at the same time each block the password from a container of their own

g.text: Given a project that scans in Docker holds a synthetic password, committed and staged
A project generated with the default answers. Its .config/betterleaks/Taskfile.yml keeps TASK_BETTERLEAKS_MODE at
"docker", so every scan starts a container.
Since the main branch, a commit adds src/service.js with a synthetic password on line 1. A second line with the same

text.tspan: grep TASK_BETTERLEAKS_MODE .config/betterleaks/Taskfile.yml && git diff origin/main HEAD -- src/service.js && git

g.text: Then two full scans started at the same time both block the password, each from its own
Two full scans start together. Each one runs betterleaks in a container named betterleaks-container followed by an id of
its own, and removes only that container when it ends.
Both find the two lines, print "REDACTED" where the password was, and fail with "❌ Betterleaks detected secrets in your
code!". The test also starts two staged scans and two branch scans together, and each of them blocks the password too.
